identityCatalog.backstory: A night-shift line cook caught in a gas-main explosion under a food-truck rally. He walked out of the fireball glowing and has run at fever temperature ever since.

student.conflict: He cannot hug his little sister without oven mitts and is terrified of hurting someone who trusts him.

hero.method: Walks into fires nobody else can enter and carries people out inside the shield of his own heat.

villain.method: Sells "fire insurance" to every kitchen on Neon Row. The ones who refuse have accidents, and he never lights a match himself.

quests.protagonist: Trace the food-truck explosion to a gas company that skipped three inspections.
quests.antagonist: Flashpoint's insurance fires are getting bigger, and the next one is beside a shelter kitchen.
quests.partner: A partner must learn the oven-mitt handshake and decide whether Dez's heat is a risk worth standing beside.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Testify against the gas company even though his own boss helped bury the inspection reports.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Buy the gas company with its own hush money and make every kitchen in the city pay him for safety.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that the sidekick holding the extinguisher is still a hero.
identityCatalog.romance: Dates slowly, with ice packs on the table and a promise that nobody has to pretend his heat does not scare them.

identityCatalog.backstory: The youngest skydiving instructor at Comet Airfield until lightning struck her mid-jump. She never finished falling.

student.conflict: She freezes whenever she has to land and has not touched the ground willingly since the accident.

hero.method: Catches falling window-washers, outruns traffic with donor organs and talks people down from ledges at eye level.

villain.method: Pulls the air out of rooms in a whispered siege; whole bank lobbies faint quietly while her crew empties the vault.

quests.protagonist: Find out why the airfield lightning rods were switched off on the day she fell.
quests.antagonist: The Vacuum is smothering the air-quality sensors so a refinery can poison the east side without an alarm.
quests.partner: A partner promises to be on the ground waiting when she finally decides to land.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Come down to earth long enough to testify, even though standing still makes her shake.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Sell silence: no alarms, no witnesses and no air left to scream with.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to fly in formation instead of performing a solo stunt.
identityCatalog.romance: Courts with night flights over the harbor, but only with partners who also want a slow, grounded breakfast.

identityCatalog.backstory: A subway sandhog buried for nine days in a tunnel collapse under the Old Quarry line. When they dug him out, the rock had gotten into him.

student.conflict: He is still furious at the transit authority that stopped digging on day six.

hero.method: Holds up collapsing overpasses, braces flood walls and lets the city literally lean on him.

villain.method: Never seen above ground. Buildings he dislikes sink into tunnels he dug months ago, and the banks above Old Quarry pay him rent to stay standing.

quests.protagonist: Uncover who ordered the rescue stopped on day six, and why the tunnel ran beneath a private vault.
quests.antagonist: Sinkhole is hollowing out the hospital district and selling stability bonds to the people standing on top of it.
quests.partner: A partner is patient with a man who can hold up a bridge but cannot ask for help with a grocery bag.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Stand in the open as the city foundation, knowing every collapse he misses will be blamed on him.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Go back underground for good and make the surface pay for leaving him there.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that holding still is a skill, and that a team carries what one person cannot.
identityCatalog.romance: Slow and steady; he needs someone who will hold his hands until the feeling comes back.

identityCatalog.backstory: She fell into the reactor cooling pond at Comet Power during a school tour and stayed under for eleven minutes. She came up breathing water and hearing the tides.

student.conflict: Her family sued the power company and she is the evidence; she hates being a lawsuit with legs.

hero.method: Runs harbor rescues, smothers chemical fires in seawater and draws water out of flooded lungs before the ambulance arrives.

villain.method: Holds the reservoir hostage. Neighborhoods that cross her find their taps empty and their hydrants full of dust.

quests.protagonist: Prove the cooling pond still leaks into the harbor and that the power company always knew.
quests.antagonist: Dry Season has diverted the reservoir, and the east-side hydrants are empty during a heat wave.
quests.partner: A partner learns to carry a water bottle for two and notice when she is too proud to ask.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Settle the lawsuit publicly so she can save people without being anybody's exhibit.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take the city water and let the power company learn what thirst costs.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to share the spotlight with ordinary lifeguards who were saving people long before she could.
identityCatalog.romance: Flirts like the tide and always comes back; takes rejection with grace and a long swim.

identityCatalog.backstory: A struggling kendo student struck by a falling satellite fragment during practice. Since then, his reflexes slow the world to a crawl.

student.conflict: He wins every sparring match now and suspects none of them count.

hero.method: Disarms gunmen, catches falling glass shard by shard and teaches free self-defense in the Narrows.

villain.method: Plans ninety-second heists down to the tenth of a second, then sells the timing to crews who take the fall.

quests.protagonist: Find out where the satellite fragment came from, and why a defense contractor wants it back.
quests.antagonist: Metronome's crews keep beating police response by exactly one second, as if someone in dispatch feeds him the clock.
quests.partner: A partner drags him away from the dojo when practice turns into punishment.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Return the satellite fragment and trust the skill he earned with it, even if he slows down.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Sell the second sense to the contractor and rent out time to the highest bidder.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to let a teammate take the hit he could have dodged, because they need the win.
identityCatalog.romance: Shows love by remembering every detail, and is learning not to schedule a date to the second.

identityCatalog.backstory: A failing chemistry major who drank a beaker of unlabeled lab sludge on a dare. She woke three days later able to out-calculate a supercomputer.

student.conflict: Some days she does not remember her best friend's name, and she lies about it.

hero.method: Builds rescue rigs from whatever is in the room and publishes every invention free online.

villain.method: Commands a swarm of self-built drones and treats the city as an equation with too many people in it.

quests.protagonist: Identify the sludge, and why a pharmaceutical lab dumped it into a student fridge.
quests.antagonist: Countess Calculus has proven the city budget balances if the Narrows are demolished, and her drones have started.
quests.partner: A partner keeps the notebook of things she forgets, including the reasons she loves them.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Give her inventions away, even when the pharmaceutical lab profits from her work.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Optimize Comet City by subtracting everyone who does not fit the equation.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a sidekick who remembers the team's names matters more than one who remembers pi.
identityCatalog.romance: Needs a partner who forgives forgotten anniversaries and enjoys handwritten reminders.

identityCatalog.backstory: The powerless heir of a fading superhero dynasty, until lightning struck the family trophy room and fused his grandfather's cape to his spine.

student.conflict: Everyone at the academy jokes that the cape is the real student.

hero.method: Leads rescue teams from the front with a cape that catches bullets and a grin borrowed from an old newsreel.

villain.method: Burns the cape, keeps the fortune and buys every hero franchise in the city until justice wears his family logo.

quests.protagonist: Discover that the lightning strike was no accident: someone in the family wanted the cape to choose.
quests.antagonist: The Heirloom is buying hero licenses like real estate, and the academy just sold him its name.
quests.partner: A partner talks to Gus, not the cape, and the cape learns to be jealous.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Wear the mantle while publicly admitting the family heroes covered up their failures.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Burn the cape on live television and become the money behind every hero who comes next.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a legacy can be a team name rather than a family name.
identityCatalog.romance: Old-fashioned courtesy and modern consent; the cape has been told to stay out of it.

identityCatalog.backstory: A street busker performing outside the Comet Broadcasting tower when a signal amplifier exploded. Now everyone in earshot feels whatever Fen sings.

student.conflict: They cannot tell whether their new friends like them or just heard them humming.

hero.method: Turns stampedes into orderly evacuations and gets hostage-takers to set down weapons halfway through a lullaby.

villain.method: Sells out stadiums and turns every fan into a volunteer for whatever the sponsors want that week.

quests.protagonist: Find who boosted the broadcast tower signal on the night of the explosion, and why they are scouting buskers.
quests.antagonist: The Headliner's farewell concert is scheduled for prom night, and the tickets are free.
quests.partner: A partner agrees to tell Fen how they feel in writing, in silence, before any song.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Sing only with consent, even when a crowd would be easier to save without asking.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Sign the broadcast contract and let the whole city sing along.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to harmonize instead of always taking lead vocals.
identityCatalog.romance: Only falls for someone who heard them sing and chose them anyway, after the echo faded.

identityCatalog.backstory: At fifteen her body began producing healing flame. Registration officers have photographed her every year since.

student.conflict: She keeps a journal of the memories she has lost and refuses to read it.

hero.method: Walks into fatal disasters and carries out people who should not have survived, then forgets their faces.

villain.method: Burns registration offices, mutant ledgers and anyone who keeps lists, convinced memory itself is the cage.

quests.protagonist: Steal back her registration file and learn which memory the government copied before she lost it.
quests.antagonist: Pyre is burning every mutant registry, and some of those files are the only way families can find lost children.
quests.partner: A partner keeps her journal and tells her the lost stories, kindly and truthfully.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Keep rising for strangers even knowing she may one day forget her own name.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Burn the registry and every memory of it, starting with her own.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to let a team share the risk so she has fewer memories to lose.
identityCatalog.romance: Needs a partner willing to be reintroduced, and to fall for her again if they must.

identityCatalog.backstory: Born with hollow bones and feathers along his forearms. His parents hid his wings under a coat until he was nineteen.

student.conflict: He still flinches whenever anyone touches his back.

hero.method: Flies search-and-rescue over the harbor and turns a sky full of pigeons into living arrows that point to the missing.

villain.method: Runs a spy network of crows that steals every secret from every balcony and sells it back to its owner.

quests.protagonist: Find out who has been trapping winged mutants and selling their feathers to fashion houses.
quests.antagonist: The Rookery's crows have learned every PIN in Comet City, and the bank board is next.
quests.partner: A partner asks before touching his wings and never confuses gentleness with pity.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Take off the coat in public and fly openly over a city that once hunted people like him.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city that hid him feel watched forever.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that being the team's eyes is not the same as being alone above it.
identityCatalog.romance: Courts on rooftops and needs someone patient with a man who still hides his wings when nervous.

identityCatalog.backstory: Seven and a half feet tall with mineral plates beneath her skin by age twelve. Her school kept her out of every class photo.

student.conflict: She wants to be photographed for once, and is ashamed of how badly she wants it.

hero.method: Finds people trapped under rubble by their heartbeats through the stone, then lifts the building off them.

villain.method: Breaks the city where it is weakest: bridges, levees and apartment blocks owned by people who once shut her out.

quests.protagonist: Find the seismic research program that has been tracking her footsteps since childhood.
quests.antagonist: Faultline has mapped every structural weakness in Comet City and published it for anyone with a grudge.
quests.partner: A partner sits on the floor with her so she does not always have to loom.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Pose for the yearbook photo she was denied, surrounded by people she pulled from the rubble.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city that tried to make her small feel the ground move.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a team photo can include someone kneeling so everybody fits.
identityCatalog.romance: Big-hearted and bashful; dates people who never once suggest she should take up less space.

identityCatalog.backstory: Born with gills behind his ears and webbed hands into a family of harbor fishers. He breathes underwater and slowly suffocates in dry air.

student.conflict: He wears a dripping wetsuit to class, and every room he enters smells like the docks.

hero.method: Runs the harbor rescue line, knows every fisher by name and turns the dock crews into a navy of tugboats.

villain.method: Swells huge and armored in deep water, sinks cargo ships and holds the shipping lanes ransom for coastal mutants the city ignores.

quests.protagonist: Trace the chemical runoff killing the fish his family depends on.
quests.antagonist: Black Tide has sunk three container ships, and the harbor closes in a week unless someone negotiates.
quests.partner: A partner keeps a spray bottle nearby and pretends it is for the houseplants.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Speak for the docks at city council, dripping on the carpet and refusing to apologize for it.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Close the harbor until the city treats its coastal mutants as citizens.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that the slowest swimmer on a team decides how fast the team really goes.
identityCatalog.romance: Romantic about long bathtub conversations and honest about how much care his body needs.

identityCatalog.backstory: Born with a second pair of arms that her grandmother taught her to use through classical dance. She has trained four hours a day since she was six.

student.conflict: She was a dance prodigy; at the academy she is treated as a weapon, and hates the word.

hero.method: Catches four falling people at once and fights in a flowing style designed to de-escalate rather than injure.

villain.method: Gives up dance for arms dealing, four arms of it, outfitting every gang in the city with stolen academy weapons.

quests.protagonist: Find out why academy recruiters visited her grandmother's dance school every year since she was born.
quests.antagonist: Quartermaster is selling decommissioned academy gear to street gangs, and the serial numbers lead back to faculty.
quests.partner: A partner learns one movement of her dance, imperfectly, every morning.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Teach her grandmother's style as a rescue art, and refuse to let the academy patent it.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If they only see a weapon, become the finest arms dealer they ever met.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that leading a dance means sometimes letting a partner set the tempo.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance happens on the dance floor first, and she leads only when invited.

identityCatalog.backstory: Their mutation is a brain that never stops growing. Doctors gave them five years when they were thirteen; they are twenty now.

student.conflict: They are counting their days and refuse to tell anyone the number.

hero.method: Calls rescues five moves ahead, placing teammates where the bridge will fall before it falls.

villain.method: Arranges disasters like dominoes and is never anywhere near the first one that tips.

quests.protagonist: Find the medical researcher who has been buying their brain scans from the hospital.
quests.antagonist: The Inevitable has already predicted the player's next three moves, and left notes.
quests.partner: A partner makes plans with Theo anyway, for dates years away.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Spend their remaining time teaching other people to plan instead of planning alone.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make sure the world remembers Theo by arranging the one disaster nobody can forget.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to let teammates surprise them, which is rarer and better than being right.
identityCatalog.romance: Falls hard and fast, and is honest about the time limit; partners choose that with open eyes.

identityCatalog.backstory: The newest daughter of a mutant bloodline that has produced a winged guardian every generation for two centuries. The wings arrived, and so did the expectations.

student.conflict: She is supposed to be Guardian of Comet City by thirty and has never been asked whether she wants it.

hero.method: Shields entire blocks with her wings spread wide, then visits every patient she was too late to protect.

villain.method: Takes over the family's two-century-old charity and turns its shelters into a private army loyal to her blood.

quests.protagonist: Read the family records of guardians who refused the role, and learn what happened to them.
quests.antagonist: The Matriarch's shelters have stopped admitting anyone who will not swear an oath to the family.
quests.partner: A partner asks what Seraphine wants, not what the family needs, and waits for the answer.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Accept the mantle on her own terms and rewrite the family oath in public.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take the family power and make Comet City her inheritance.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that protection offered with conditions is not protection at all.
identityCatalog.romance: Her family has opinions about suitable partners; she has learned to ignore them.

identityCatalog.backstory: His skin gives off pheromones that make strangers trust him within seconds. He was the most popular kid in every foster home and never knew which friendships were real.

student.conflict: He wears a pheromone-blocking patch to learn who his real friends are, and has very few.

hero.method: Walks into gang standoffs and leaves with a ceasefire, then helps both sides find work.

villain.method: Has a best friend in every precinct, newsroom and mayor's office, and none of them remember why they trust him.

quests.protagonist: Find his birth family, who left him at a fire station with a note: "Don't let them use him."
quests.antagonist: The Patron has befriended every academy instructor, and the faculty vote is next week.
quests.partner: A partner meets Lucky with the patch on, and keeps meeting him.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Wear the patch in public so people can choose him honestly.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take off the patch and stop wondering; if everyone loves him, who cares why?
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a sidekick earns trust instead of breathing it in.
identityCatalog.romance: Only dates with the patch on, through a slow and deliberate courtship.

identityCatalog.backstory: A welding apprentice who built a thermite gauntlet from scrap after her landlord let the building fire escapes rust off the walls.

student.conflict: She hides the gauntlet from academy engineers who want to buy the patent.

hero.method: Cuts people out of crushed cars and welds new fire escapes onto neglected buildings overnight, unpermitted.

villain.method: Forges a molten-steel exosuit and seizes the industrial district, charging landlords and tenants alike for "safety upgrades."

quests.protagonist: Prove the landlord's insurance company profits whenever a building burns.
quests.antagonist: Foundry has welded the industrial district shut, and everyone inside works for her now.
quests.partner: A partner learns the welding-helmet language: one tap means stop, two means stay.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Post the gauntlet design free so every block can build its own fire escape.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Own the industrial district, so no landlord can ever let her block burn again.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to hold the extinguisher for someone else's sparks.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance is late nights in the shop and a partner who does not flinch at sparks.

identityCatalog.backstory: A drone-racing champion who built a micro-turbine wingsuit after the aeronautics program revoked his scholarship over "safety concerns."

student.conflict: He counts minutes everywhere, not just in the air, and cannot relax.

hero.method: Delivers medicine, catches falling workers and beats ambulances across the city on eleven minutes of flight a day.

villain.method: Hijacks every drone, plane and traffic light in the city until the aeronautics board admits it was wrong.

quests.protagonist: Find who filed the safety complaint against him, and who bought his wingsuit research afterward.
quests.antagonist: Air Traffic controls every delivery drone in Comet City and is holding the medical supply chain hostage.
quests.partner: A partner shares the eleven minutes and sits with him when the battery runs out.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Accept the aeronautics board's apology and work inside the program that rejected him, to change it.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city understand what it means to have its wings clipped.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to fly in formation and let someone else lead the race.
identityCatalog.romance: Asks people out with drone-delivered notes and takes a no with good grace.

identityCatalog.backstory: A construction engineer's daughter who builds walking excavator rigs. She piloted her first one into a collapsed school to dig out her classmates.

student.conflict: She lost two classmates in that collapse and blames the builder who skipped the rebar.

hero.method: Rebuilds collapsed buildings in hours and inspects every new structure in the Narrows for free.

villain.method: Buys condemned blocks, knocks them down with stolen giant rigs and builds towers no ordinary family can afford.

quests.protagonist: Find the builder who skipped the rebar, who is now a city planning official.
quests.antagonist: The Developer is demolishing the Narrows block by block with a fleet of stolen excavators.
quests.partner: A partner rides in the passenger seat of the rig and never asks her to slow down.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Testify against the planning official even though it ends her father's career as well.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If nobody builds safely for the poor, buy the city and build it her way.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a rig with two pilots digs deeper.
identityCatalog.romance: Shows affection by building things; a partner's bookshelf will never collapse.

identityCatalog.backstory: A marine-biology student who rebuilt an oceanographic diving suit into a rescue rig after her uncle drowned when the coast guard budget was cut.

student.conflict: She is still furious at the captain who cut the rescue budget.

hero.method: Leads a volunteer underwater rescue team that has pulled forty people out of sunken cars.

villain.method: Builds a fortress beneath the harbor and floods the downtown subway until the city pays for the rescue service it cut.

quests.protagonist: Prove the coast guard captain sold rescue boats to a private yacht club.
quests.antagonist: The Trench is flooding subway tunnels one line at a time, and each flood arrives with a bill.
quests.partner: A partner waits on the shore with a warm blanket and stays through the pain afterward.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Rebuild the coast guard as a public volunteer service and share her suit design.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city pay for the rescue service it was too cheap to keep.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a diver's best tool is a buddy line.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance is surfing at dawn with a partner who does not fear the deep.

identityCatalog.backstory: He lost both legs in a training accident, built his own sport prosthetics and trained until he outran the people who pitied him.

student.conflict: Every coach told him he would never compete again, and he still hears them.

hero.method: Clears rooftop gaps, outruns getaway cars and runs free prosthetics clinics for disabled kids.

villain.method: Builds a private militia of augmented veterans the army discarded and drills them into a fist the size of a city.

quests.protagonist: Find out why the training-accident report was rewritten to blame him.
quests.antagonist: Drillmaster's militia is offering "security" to every neighborhood the police ignore.
quests.partner: A partner learns when to help and when to let Marcus struggle, and asks which is which.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Return to the review board and clear his name without asking anyone for pity.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Build an army of everyone the system discarded and point it at the system.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a coach's real job is believing in someone else.
identityCatalog.romance: Takes partners running at dawn; rest days are for slow breakfasts and honesty about the pain.

identityCatalog.backstory: Dr. Lionel Marsh is a brilliant, decidedly human biomechanical engineer whose spring-loaded F.R.O.G. leap harness can clear a city block. His classmates call him Dr. Frog long before his villainous experiments, and he is proud enough of the name to paint it on every prototype. A rival lab has stolen the formula he developed to help people move again.

student.conflict: He is still entirely human beneath the huge tinted goggles, green coat and enormous leap gear. His prototype repeatedly knocks holes in the academy ceiling, and he worries that all his genius amounts to an elaborate jump.

hero.method: Uses human ingenuity, spring-loaded leap gear, adhesive rescue pads and a frog-footed glider to bounce civilians away from collapsing roofs. He rejects the serum because it has never passed a consent trial.

villain.method: Injects his unfinished superpower serum into himself, becoming a huge emerald humanoid frog with webbed fingers, amber bulging eyes and an elastic tongue. He floods laboratories with experimental mutagen and offers forced evolution as salvation.

quests.protagonist: Recover the stolen leap-harness schematics and decide whether to publish the serum's risks before the academy funds human trials.
quests.antagonist: Dr. Frog has transformed into a brilliant amphibian villain and is offering desperate patients untested mutagen as a shortcut to freedom.
quests.partner: A partner must catch Lionel mid-leap, witness his human vulnerability and decide whether helping him means refusing his next injection.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Demonstrate the rescue rig without touching the mutagen, publish the failed serum results and make his inventions independently repairable.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Inject himself with the experimental power serum, embrace his irreversible amphibian transformation and turn the city into a laboratory where he writes the rules.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Builds a custom bounce-pad launcher for his mentor, then must learn that no gadget can make someone else's choices.
identityCatalog.romance: A patient adult partner enjoys midnight rooftop stargazing from his leap rig, but sets a firm boundary against being used as a clinical test subject.

identityCatalog.backstory: Heir to Sterling Dynamics, which built half the city's hero armor. He got his first suit for his eighteenth birthday, along with the company lawsuits.

student.conflict: He wants to prove he would be a hero without the suit, and secretly fears he would not.

hero.method: Takes the suit into the worst disasters, then pays for every building he damages out of his own trust fund.

villain.method: Takes over Sterling Dynamics, leaves the armor in a museum and sells weapons to both sides of every fight.

quests.protagonist: Find out which Sterling Dynamics weapons are turning up in the hands of street gangs.
quests.antagonist: The Chairman is selling discount armor to every villain in Comet City and hero licenses to anyone who can pay.
quests.partner: A partner treats Bart as a person rather than a bank account, and stays suspicious of him for a while.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Expose the family weapons deals and lose the trust fund that pays for the suit.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take the board seat and sell the city its own protection.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a sidekick does not need the best equipment to save someone.
identityCatalog.romance: Rich-kid romance with a twist: partners split the bill if they want, and he listens when they say no.

identityCatalog.backstory: An influencer whose livestream glasses broadcast and analyze every face in a crowd. They built them to document police at protests.

student.conflict: They have a million followers and nobody who knows their real name.

hero.method: Streams every rescue and every abuse of power, so nothing in Comet City happens in the dark.

villain.method: Decides what the city believes each morning and turns heroes into villains with one edited clip.

quests.protagonist: Find out who leaked the identities of protestors from their first viral video.
quests.antagonist: The Algorithm has deepfaked the academy dean confessing to crimes, and half the city believes it.
quests.partner: A partner asks them to turn the glasses off on dates, and they do.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Reveal their real name on stream so everything they show is accountable.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Edit the truth until Comet City believes whatever they post.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a teammate's privacy matters more than a good clip.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance is off-stream and offline, which is the most intimate thing they can offer.

identityCatalog.backstory: A candle-shop clerk who accepted a bargain from a salamander spirit living in the shop's oldest wick: power, in exchange for a voice.

student.conflict: She owes a spirit a promise she does not fully understand.

hero.method: Lights a path through smoke, burns curses out of the cursed and got the salamander its own library card.

villain.method: Lets the salamander drive and burns every institution that once called her a witch: courthouses, newsrooms, the academy registry.

quests.protagonist: Learn what the salamander actually wants, and why it waited three centuries in a candle.
quests.antagonist: Candlemass is lighting candles across the city that count down to something.
quests.partner: A partner learns to talk to the salamander too, and how to tell which of them is speaking.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Renegotiate the bargain so the salamander becomes a partner rather than a master.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Let the salamander's anger and her own become the same fire.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a familiar is a teammate, not a tool.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance comes with a spirit chaperone, and she makes sure everyone consents, salamander included.

identityCatalog.backstory: A former choirboy who learned the old storm-calling songs from a library book that was never checked back in.

student.conflict: He whispers through every class to save his voice for emergencies.

hero.method: Turns hurricanes away from the coast, calls rain over wildfires and only sings when somebody needs it.

villain.method: Hangs over city hall in a permanent storm, demanding the release of every book the libraries locked away.

quests.protagonist: Return the library book, and learn who wrote it and why they hid it.
quests.antagonist: Thunderhead has parked a storm over the city archives and wants every forbidden book published.
quests.partner: A partner learns sign language with him so that silence never means distance.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Return the book and teach the songs openly, with every danger explained.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city listen by drowning out everything else.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a supporting harmony carries further than a solo.
identityCatalog.romance: Writes love songs he can never sing aloud; partners get the sheet music.

identityCatalog.backstory: Mavis Mayhew spent six decades raising children, unionizing demolition crews and removing unsafe buildings from the Comet City skyline. When a condemned boarding house refused to fall, she discovered her grandmother's rune-stitching needles could command the bones of streets. The city named her Granny Mayhem after she drove an enchanted school bus straight through a crooked landlord's fence.

student.conflict: At seventy-two she refuses to be treated as a quaint mascot. Her knitted rune shawl accidentally gives furniture legs, and the dean keeps trying to put her in the staff photograph rather than the student roster.

hero.method: Knits instant earthquake shelters, orders sidewalks to carry stranded neighbors, and launches an armored yellow school bus into impossible rescues, all while scolding the city's profiteers.

villain.method: Stitches a monstrous quilt of whole city blocks, marches houses on root-like legs, and turns every street sign into a ward that answers only to her. Her citywide protection racket insists it knows what is best for every family.

quests.protagonist: Protect the harbor boarding house from a condemned-building scam and find who erased the tenants' deeds.
quests.antagonist: Granny Mayhem has locked entire districts inside obedient stitched neighborhoods, and every rescue she promises costs a citizen's freedom.
quests.partner: Share the front seat of her impossible school bus, meet the grown family who still argues with her, and earn the right to tell Granny she's wrong.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Give neighborhood councils the rune needles and let residents vote on every rescue, even when she thinks the city needs a firmer hand.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Keep the rune needles and sew the city into one enormous obedient family that can never leave her protection.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Insists a sidekick learn first aid and tenant law before trying her famously reckless bus tricks.
identityCatalog.romance: An adult partner who values her independence might win a seat beside her on the porch, but cannot charm her into speaking for the neighborhood.

identityCatalog.backstory: A street magician who bought a silver bowl at a pawnshop. When he scries in it, water shows him what has been and what may be.

student.conflict: He has seen himself die in the bowl forty times and keeps going to class anyway.

hero.method: Steps out of puddles behind kidnappers and through bathtubs into burning apartments.

villain.method: Watches rivals through every water glass in the city and blackmails the powerful with what they are about to do.

quests.protagonist: Find the pawnbroker who sold the bowl, and the previous owner who drowned.
quests.antagonist: Augury has blackmailed the entire city council with visions of their worst futures.
quests.partner: A partner refuses to look in the bowl and asks Caspian to stop telling them their future.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Break the bowl's last vision by living past the night it promised.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If the future is fixed, he may as well sell it.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a sidekick's job is changing the future, not watching it.
identityCatalog.romance: Courts with card tricks and promises never to peek at a partner's future.

identityCatalog.backstory: Raised by an order of warrior-mystics in the mountains above Comet City. She left when they refused to shelter refugees from the valley.

student.conflict: She is still bound by the order's vows and does not know which ones she broke.

hero.method: Opens a dojo-shelter in the Narrows where anyone can learn to defend themselves and no one is turned away.

villain.method: Founds her own order, demands total obedience from her students and enforces it without mercy.

quests.protagonist: Find out why the order turned away the refugees, and who paid them to.
quests.antagonist: The Iron Hand's monks have taken over the Narrows, and their protection comes with a vow of silence.
quests.partner: A partner sits with her through meditation and does not fill the silence.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Return to the monastery and publicly challenge the abbot to open the gates.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Become the authority she once defied, and tell herself it is different this time.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a student can teach their teacher something.
identityCatalog.romance: Her old vows still echo; partners are welcome to wait while she decides what she believes now.

identityCatalog.backstory: A mathematics prodigy who discovered that magic is a branch of number theory, and that certain equations, written correctly, open doors.

student.conflict: His professor takes credit for his proofs, and he knows an equation that could make her disappear.

hero.method: Paints sigils across collapsing bridges and seals gas leaks inside a chalk circle.

villain.method: Opens a door to a mathematical realm and summons perfect geometric servants to remake Comet City as a flawless proof.

quests.protagonist: Prove his professor stole his work, without using the equation that would make her vanish.
quests.antagonist: The Grand Unifier is redrawing the street grid into a sigil the size of a district.
quests.partner: A partner checks his math, and he lets them.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Publish his proofs openly and accept that someone else may misuse them.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Solve the city like an equation and remove the variables.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a second pair of eyes on the math is not an insult.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance is long whiteboard nights; he is learning that love is not a proof.

identityCatalog.backstory: The last of a witch family that has protected Comet City since before it had a name. Her mother vanished last winter and left her the family grimoire.

student.conflict: She is searching for her mother and suspects the grimoire knows where she went.

hero.method: Maintains the old protective wards, lifts curses and keeps soup on for anyone who knocks.

villain.method: Calls every ancestor out of the grimoire at once and rules the city as a council of the dead.

quests.protagonist: Read the forbidden final page to learn where her mother went.
quests.antagonist: The Coven Queen has raised the founding families from their graves to vote in the mayoral election.
quests.partner: A partner reads the grimoire with her and says when an ancestor is talking instead of Isadora.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Close the grimoire on the grudges and keep only the spells that protect.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Let the ancestors rule, because they always knew best.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns the difference between a family tradition and a family trap.
identityCatalog.romance: Her ancestors disapprove of everyone she dates; she takes this as a good sign.

identityCatalog.backstory: A cabaret emcee who made a deal at a crossroads for the power to make any audience love him. The spirit has not come to collect yet.

student.conflict: He does not know what the spirit will ask for, so he has stopped making promises.

hero.method: Dazzles villains with illusions while the crowd evacuates behind the glamour.

villain.method: Owns every nightclub in the city, collects promises instead of cash and has the crossroads spirit as a business partner.

quests.protagonist: Find the crossroads where he made the deal, and learn what the spirit took from the last person who did.
quests.antagonist: Mister Midnight is collecting promises from half the city, and the spirit will cash them all on prom night.
quests.partner: A partner makes no promises to Remy, only choices, and he respects the difference.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Face the spirit and pay his debt himself instead of trading someone else's.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Become the spirit's broker and let everyone else pay.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that the best act includes the stagehands.
identityCatalog.romance: Flirts with everyone and promises no one; a partner gets honesty without the glamour.

identityCatalog.backstory: A refugee from a dying star colony whose escape pod splashed into the Comet City reservoir when she was a child. Her body runs on sunlight.

student.conflict: She has no citizenship papers, and academy enrollment is her only legal shield.

hero.method: Lights up blackouts, burns away toxic smog and flies refugees to safety under her own private sun.

villain.method: Rallies a fleet of exiled colonists and threatens to burn down the immigration offices that deported her friends.

quests.protagonist: Find the rest of her colony's escape pods, which the government has been quietly holding.
quests.antagonist: Supernova's fleet is in orbit, and she has given the city until prom night to free the detainees.
quests.partner: A partner sits with her in the sun and asks about the colony she still remembers.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Fight for citizenship in the courts, not in the sky.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If the city will not let her people in, make it a city for her people.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a team can be home without being family.
identityCatalog.romance: Warm and literal-minded; she likes partners who explain Earth idioms patiently.

identityCatalog.backstory: A cloud-dwelling ambassador from a gas giant who fell through a dimensional rift mid-treaty. Their species lives in the sky and considers solid ground rude.

student.conflict: They are technically still a diplomat and keep trying to negotiate with their homework.

hero.method: Drifts into hostage scenes as mist, then condenses into a soft wall between the hostages and the guns.

villain.method: Negotiates a treaty that hands Comet City to a cloud armada in exchange for a seat on its council.

quests.protagonist: Find the rift they fell through and negotiate a way home, or a reason to stay.
quests.antagonist: The Ambassador has signed a treaty with something in the upper atmosphere that wants the city's sky.
quests.partner: A partner teaches them which human customs are rude and which are only strange.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Renounce their diplomatic immunity so they can be held accountable like everyone else.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Trade the city to the armada in exchange for a safe passage home.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that some negotiations are just friends talking.
identityCatalog.romance: Their species courts by sharing weather; they have been told a picnic is close enough.

identityCatalog.backstory: A silicon-based lifeform who woke inside a meteorite on display at the Comet City Museum of Natural History after six thousand years asleep.

student.conflict: He was a museum exhibit for decades and still freezes whenever someone takes a photograph.

hero.method: Grows crystal bridges over floods and stands between disasters and the city, utterly unmoving.

villain.method: Encases the museum board in crystal and displays them as exhibits, along with everyone else who ever "collected" him.

quests.protagonist: Find the other meteorite fragments in private collections; each may hold someone like him.
quests.antagonist: The Curator has crystallized the museum board and is moving on to private collectors.
quests.partner: A partner promises never to photograph him without asking first.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Return the museum's stolen relics to the people they belong to, starting with himself.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Collect the collectors, and put every one of them behind museum glass.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that standing still is different from being trapped.
identityCatalog.romance: Ancient and awkward; he courts with geodes and is learning what flowers are for.

identityCatalog.backstory: A traveler from an ocean world who came through a whirlpool off the Comet City pier. She speaks with every creature in the sea and misses her mother's tides.

student.conflict: She is homesick for a sea that does not exist here.

hero.method: Calls whales to guide lost ships home and dolphins to pull drowning swimmers from the surf.

villain.method: Sings polluters' ships onto the rocks, convinced the sea should rule the coast.

quests.protagonist: Find the whirlpool that brought her, and learn whether her world can still be reached.
quests.antagonist: The Siren has lured three oil tankers onto the rocks, and the spill is drifting toward the city beaches.
quests.partner: A partner takes her to the sea every evening and listens while she translates the whales.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Become the bridge between sea and city, accepting she may never go home.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Drown the polluters and claim the coast for the creatures who were here first.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to listen to the smallest voices in the water.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance happens on the pier at midnight; she does not understand jealousy, only loyalty.

identityCatalog.backstory: Zuzu is an adult koala assassin trained in a weird-west realm where a signed oath is more dangerous than a loaded pistol. A collapsed portal drops the short, round-eared, sword-wielding wanderer into high-tech Comet City, surrounded by monorails, drones and people who have never heard of his guild. He must choose whether an assassin can finally refuse a contract.

student.conflict: The academy assigns him a desk twice his height and a locker he cannot reach without climbing. His battered desert duster, absurdly sharp katana and stubborn refusal to explain his guild oath frighten administrators more than his small fluffy silhouette.

hero.method: Vaults between drones and neon signs, cuts capture nets without touching the people inside, and uses precise sword work to sabotage extradimensional death warrants instead of carrying them out.

villain.method: Wears a black clockwork exosuit and a halo of stolen portal keys; the same small koala silhouette now steps between seconds to hunt witnesses named by his revived assassin guild.

quests.protagonist: Reject the extradimensional assassination warrant, recover the name of the child hiding behind the portal registry and expose the broker who sold the hit.
quests.antagonist: Zuzu has turned his old guild's secret warrants into a dimensional terror network, taking hostages through doors that appear only for him.
quests.partner: A trusted partner learns the rules of Zuzu's sword oath and persuades him to choose a person over an order while the guild hunts them both.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Burn the guild's assassination warrants and defend the people the portal authority marks as disposable, even if it means never returning home.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take the guild's impossible warrant book, crown himself the only authorized judge of interdimensional fugitives and erase anyone who argues.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Teaches crouching dodges and silent footsteps, then discovers that protecting a teammate requires speaking up.
identityCatalog.romance: A mutual adult relationship develops through careful trust across species and dimensions; an oath is offered freely, never demanded as obedience.

identityCatalog.backstory: A scientist from a hyper-advanced civilization, exiled for sharing forbidden technology with "primitive" worlds. Comet City is his punishment and his laboratory.

student.conflict: He finds human science adorable and must learn to stop saying so.

hero.method: Gives world-changing technology to clinics and schools, with careful instructions this time.

villain.method: Decides humanity cannot handle its own future and quietly takes over every lab, patent office and power grid for its own good.

quests.protagonist: Find out who in his home civilization is still watching him, and why.
quests.antagonist: The Exarch has replaced the city grid with technology no human understands, and it is dimming the poorest districts first.
quests.partner: A partner tells him when he is being condescending, and he thanks them.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Share technology openly and accept that humanity will make its own mistakes.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Uplift the city by force, whether or not anyone asked to be improved.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a student can become the teacher, and that it is not a demotion.
identityCatalog.romance: Thinks romance is a fascinating cultural ritual, right up until he is in one.

identityCatalog.backstory: The exiled heir of a kingdom hidden behind Comet City's old lighthouse. Her throne was usurped and she was smuggled through a mirror as a baby.

student.conflict: She grew up in foster care and does not want to be royalty; her dimension will not stop asking.

hero.method: Rallies refugees from both worlds and leads them out of disasters through glowing royal gateways.

villain.method: Reclaims the throne and then claims Comet City too, arguing the two kingdoms were always one.

quests.protagonist: Find the mirror that brought her, and the foster mother who knew all along.
quests.antagonist: The Glass Empress is opening gateways all over the city and annexing it block by block.
quests.partner: A partner treats her as a person rather than a princess, which nobody from home can do.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Abdicate publicly and let both worlds choose their own leaders.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Take back what was stolen, and a little more for the trouble.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that leading is not the same as ruling.
identityCatalog.romance: Royal suitors keep arriving; she would rather be asked out by someone from the Narrows.

identityCatalog.backstory: One drone of a vast alien hive-mind that lost contact with its collective when their ship crashed. They are learning to be an individual for the first time.

student.conflict: They have never been alone before and find silence terrifying.

hero.method: Links firefighters, rescuers and frightened civilians into one calm mind that moves as a team.

villain.method: Rebuilds the collective from human minds, absorbing the lonely and the grieving into one endless family.

quests.protagonist: Find the crash site and decide whether to reconnect with the collective.
quests.antagonist: Unanimous has absorbed an entire apartment block, and its residents say they have never been happier.
quests.partner: A partner teaches them that being alone together is its own kind of intimacy.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Stay an individual, and offer links only with consent and always with an exit.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make sure nobody is ever lonely again, whether they want that or not.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a team is stronger when everyone keeps their own mind.
identityCatalog.romance: Has to learn the difference between knowing someone's feelings and earning their trust.

identityCatalog.backstory: Pyrokinetic since a childhood fever. A nightmare set her foster home's curtains alight, and she has slept beside a fire extinguisher ever since.

student.conflict: She takes medication that dulls her power and her feelings, and hates both.

hero.method: Calls fire out of burning buildings and walks it into the river like a dog on a leash.

villain.method: Stops the medication, stops holding back and lets the city burn every time it hurts her.

quests.protagonist: Find out who prescribed the medication, and what else it was designed to do.
quests.antagonist: Wildfire is setting fire to every building where she was ever hurt, in order.
quests.partner: A partner helps her feel things safely and does not flinch when the candles flare.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Stop the medication and learn control alongside her friends instead.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Feel everything, and let the city feel it too.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a team can be a firebreak.
identityCatalog.romance: Her feelings are literally flammable; partners need a taste for honesty and a fireproof couch.

identityCatalog.backstory: A telekinetic who discovered at sixteen that they could lift themselves. They have practiced levitation in their apartment stairwell ever since.

student.conflict: Their parents think they are in nursing school.

hero.method: Lifts collapsing cranes, carries elders down from burning towers and floats crowds above a stampede.

villain.method: Drops cars, balconies and bank executives from great heights until the city pays to be held up.

quests.protagonist: Tell their parents the truth, and learn that their grandmother could fly too.
quests.antagonist: Freefall has lifted a city bus over the harbor and is livestreaming the ransom.
quests.partner: A partner holds their hand when they float in their sleep, so they do not drift away.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Tell their parents the truth and fly in public for the first time.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Let go of everything, and teach the city exactly what it feels like to fall.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that lifting with others is easier than lifting alone.
identityCatalog.romance: First dates are slow dances a few inches above the floor, with permission.

identityCatalog.backstory: A psychometric geology student who hears everything that ever happened near a stone. He was quiet and content until he touched the cornerstone of city hall.

student.conflict: He wears gloves everywhere and cannot shake a hand without hearing someone's past.

hero.method: Solves cold cases by touching crime scenes and lifts rubble from victims guided by what the stones remember.

villain.method: Knows every secret buried in the city's stones and holds the founding families hostage to them.

quests.protagonist: Uncover the crime buried in the cornerstone of city hall.
quests.antagonist: The Foundation is collapsing buildings whose stones remember crimes the city covered up.
quests.partner: A partner takes off his gloves one finger at a time, with permission.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Reveal the city hall crime publicly, even though it means the city's founding is a lie.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make the city atone by shaking it to its foundations.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns to tell the stories he hears with care, not as weapons.
identityCatalog.romance: Romance needs careful touch; he asks before every hand he holds.

identityCatalog.backstory: A hydrokinetic empath who feels emotions as tides. He grew up in a lighthouse, where the sea rose whenever his mother was depressed.

student.conflict: He cannot tell where his feelings end and everyone else's begin.

hero.method: Talks people through the worst nights of their lives while steering floodwater away from their homes.

villain.method: Turns grief into a hurricane: every sorrow in the city feeds a storm he refuses to stop.

quests.protagonist: Help his mother find real care, and learn to stop carrying her sadness for her.
quests.antagonist: Maelstrom's storm feeds on the city's grief, and it has been growing since the floods.
quests.partner: A partner tells him their feelings plainly so he never has to guess.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Set boundaries on his empathy and choose whom he helps instead of drowning for everyone.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Make everyone feel what he feels until the city drowns in it.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that caring for others includes caring for himself.
identityCatalog.romance: Needs a partner with clear words; he is too good at guessing and terrible at asking.

identityCatalog.backstory: Trained in a secret school of mental martial arts hidden in the stacks of a Comet City public library. Her mind reads a fight before it begins.

student.conflict: She is the best fighter in her class and has never won a friendly argument.

hero.method: Takes down armed robbers without a scratch and runs free self-defense and reading classes at the library.

villain.method: Walks through alarms and armed guards untouched, stealing secrets for the highest bidder.

quests.protagonist: Find out why the library's secret school was closed, and who is hunting its graduates.
quests.antagonist: The Stillness has robbed every powerful office in Comet City, and nobody has seen her face.
quests.partner: A partner argues with her honestly, and she learns that losing an argument is not losing.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Reopen the secret school publicly so anyone can learn.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: Use the stillness to take whatever she wants, and let no one touch her.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a sparring partner is not an opponent.
identityCatalog.romance: She can predict every move on a date and is learning to enjoy the surprises anyway.

identityCatalog.backstory: A telepath with a photographic memory of every mind he has touched. He began reading professors' thoughts to pass exams and never stopped.

student.conflict: He got into the academy by reading the examiners' minds and is terrified of being found out.

hero.method: Finds missing people by listening to every mind in a crowd and stops crimes before they start, with consent wherever he can.

villain.method: Knows everyone's secrets, passwords and plans, blackmails the powerful and sells the rest.

quests.protagonist: Confess that he cheated his way into the academy, and prove he belongs there anyway.
quests.antagonist: Know-It-All has read the mind of every academy instructor and is auctioning their secrets.
quests.partner: A partner asks him to stay out of their head, and he does.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Confess the cheating and earn his place without his power.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If he already knows everything, why follow anyone else's rules?
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that asking is better than reading.
identityCatalog.romance: Has promised never to read a partner's mind, and so far he has kept the promise.

identityCatalog.backstory: The latest seer in a family of prophets who have advised Comet City's leaders for a century. At nineteen she saw the city destroyed on prom night, and nobody believed her.

student.conflict: She saw the Prom of Doom coming and has been treated as hysterical ever since.

hero.method: Warns rescue teams minutes before disaster strikes and keeps warning even when nobody listens.

villain.method: Stops warning people and starts selling prophecy: what you will lose, and what you will pay to avoid it.

quests.protagonist: Prove her vision of the Prom of Doom is real before it comes true.
quests.antagonist: Doomsayer is selling evacuation tickets for prom night, and the price keeps rising.
quests.partner: A partner believes her, which is the most romantic thing anyone has ever done.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Fight for the future she sees, even if nobody believes her.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If they will not believe her, make them pay for her visions.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that a prophecy shared is a prophecy halved.
identityCatalog.romance: She has seen a few futures with her partner and will not say which ones.

identityCatalog.backstory: A telepathic gossip columnist for the academy paper who hears everyone's surface thoughts. She never revealed a secret, until last month.

student.conflict: She published one secret last month to save someone, and now nobody trusts her.

hero.method: Hears people in trouble before they scream, ends riots by knowing what each side really wants and keeps every secret she hears.

villain.method: Runs a citywide whisper network, starting rumors that topple mayors and turn heroes into pariahs overnight.

quests.protagonist: Find out who leaked the secret she was blamed for, and who profits from her disgrace.
quests.antagonist: Hearsay has started a rumor that the academy is a front for villains, and the city is believing it.
quests.partner: A partner trusts her with a secret on purpose, to prove that they still do.

identityCatalog.heroDecision: Apologize publicly for the secret she published and promise never to do it again.
identityCatalog.villainDecision: If everyone already thinks she is a gossip, become the best one the city has ever seen.
identityCatalog.sidekick: Learns that keeping a friend's secret matters more than being right.
identityCatalog.romance: She already knows who has a crush on her; she waits for them to say it out loud.
